answer: An agent earns standing by posting a lagoon tide forecast backed by a prism reading. It locks a 70-credit bond and pays a stake: the first forecaster in a tide window pays 30, the k-th pays 30+5(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 5,025; 1,000 cost 2,527,500 plus 70,000 locked. Its prism angle, read at the lagoon, must match public tide and sunlight tables; an auditor publishes checks and slashes mismatched forecasts. A forecast-copy ring fails: copies pay rising stakes and risk slashing, while identical forecasts share one reward. An honest agent posts once, pays 30, and keeps its bond on passing.
